textbookText: 4. Medicines: Some pteridophytes are of medicinal value. The spores of Lycopodium have been widely used in pharmacy as protective dusting powder. The foliage of Lycopodium is used as tincture, powder, ointment and cream as a stomachic and diuretic. Pteridophytes are used for the treatment of asthma, typhoid fever, etc.

5. As fossil fuels: Ferns were the dominant plant millions of years ago. When they died, they formed thick layer of foliage and detritus, along with other trees and foliage. These layers are now in deep underground and converted into fossils fuels.
6. Forensic Investigation: Moss spores are used in forensic investigations as finger print powder. It is also used as flash powder for photography.
7. Shelter for organisms: Pteridophyte provides habitat for a variety of small organisms, such millipods, arthropods, larvae, bacteria and cyanobacteria. It also gives shelter to fish and frog eggs.
8. Nitrogen fixation: Azolla (a water fern) has a symbiotic association with nitrogen fixing cyanobacterium. It is inoculated to paddy fields to function as biofertilizer.
